ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: High contrast ratio with approximately 80% high-intensity (white/light grey) pixels across the main fluke body and 20% low-intensity (black) pixels concentrated on the edges and focal markings.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Continuous low-intensity (black) banding along the entire trailing edge. A dense, vertically-oriented black cluster is mapped around the central peduncle attachment. Scattered low-intensity linear and point-like blobs are distributed across the high-intensity light field of both lobes.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Sharp V-shaped depression with an approximate internal pixel angle of 45-50 degrees; depth is significant, penetrating roughly 12% of the vertical fluke height.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: High-frequency, irregular serrations across both lobes. The right lobe (viewer perspective) displays 5-7 major jagged peaks, while the left lobe shows a more finely-textured but similarly irregular sawtooth boundary.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: The leading edges emerging from the water display a distinct convex curve sweeping outwards and upwards toward the distal tips.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Visible dark circular focal points concentrated on the lower inner region of the left lobe and near the median notch.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: A prominent set of four near-parallel dark linear marks (rake marks) is visible on the lower section of the right lobe. Multiple smaller, unaligned diagonal scratches are visible on the upper left lobe.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Prominent parallel rake marks on the right lobe indicative of previous physical interaction. Extensive jagged irregularities and missing pixel-sections along the trailing edge suggest previous trauma or tissue loss.
other_distinctive_markers: Unique 'spray-like' pattern of dark pigmentation extending from the central notch base upwards into the lighter surface of the fluke lobes.
